title: The Experience of Crowding: A Two-Factor Theory

findings.consequent: crowding index (self-reported comfort, confinement, ill at ease, crowdedness)
findings.mechanism: High density contributes to arousal, which is then attributed to others, leading to crowding.
findings.quote: subjects felt more crowded in the small as opposed to large room

findings.consequent: crowding index (self-reported comfort, confinement, ill at ease, crowdedness)
findings.mechanism: Violations of personal space create arousal, which is attributed to others, leading to crowding.
findings.quote: in the close as opposed to far interaction distances

findings.consequent: crowding index (self-reported comfort, confinement, ill at ease, crowdedness)
findings.mechanism: Lack of attribution inhibitors (pictures) focuses attention on others, leading to attribution of arousal to them and thus increased crowding.
findings.quote: in a room without pictures as opposed to a room with pictures

findings.antecedent: high density under far interaction distance conditions
findings.consequent: crowding index (self-reported comfort, confinement, ill at ease, crowdedness)
findings.mechanism: Density's effect on crowding is more pronounced when personal space is not violated, suggesting interaction distance is the primary spatial factor for arousal.
findings.quote: density affected the experience of crowding much more under far interaction distance than under close interaction distance

findings.antecedent: addition of pictures to the room in close interaction conditions
findings.consequent: crowding index (self-reported comfort, confinement, ill at ease, crowdedness)
findings.mechanism: Pictures act as 'attribution inhibitors' by diverting attention, preventing the attribution of arousal (from personal space violation) to other people.
findings.quote: in the close interaction condition, the addition of pictures to the room significantly reduced the experience of crowding

findings.antecedent: addition of pictures to the room in far interaction conditions
findings.consequent: crowding index (self-reported comfort, confinement, ill at ease, crowdedness)
findings.mechanism: In far interaction conditions, there is no personal space violation and thus no arousal, so attribution inhibitors have no effect.
findings.quote: the far interaction condition had no effect, F < 1.

stimuli.description: Experimental rooms of two sizes (12.5 ft x 9 ft for high density, 20.5 ft x 11.5 ft for low density) with chairs arranged in a circle. Interaction distance was manipulated by chair spacing (touching for close, 19.5 inches apart for far).
Six prints and two wind chimes placed on the walls of the experimental room (picture condition) vs. bare walls (no-picture condition).

limitations: Only male subjects were included in the study, limiting generalizability to females.
The high-density (small) room was still large enough to allow some movement by subjects, potentially diluting the density effect.
The number of pictures used was chosen to avoid clutter; a different number of pictures might yield different results (e.g., increased crowding if too many).
